code_first.code:
attempts = 3
if attempts > 3 then
    print("Locked")
else
    print("Open")
endif
p: Explain the first assignment or condition that determines the output.
Test attempts=2 and explain how limiting repeated failed logins differs from preventing phishing.
code_first.a: With attempts=3, the original >3 test prints Open. Changing to >=3 correctly prints Locked. With attempts=2 it prints Open. Attempt limits reduce repeated guessing; phishing tricks users into revealing information and requires additional safeguards.

original_exam_questions: A loop runs i=0 to 4 inclusive. How many iterations execute? [2 marks]
Explain why total=1 is wrong for a plain sum accumulator. [2 marks]
Adds an unintended 1 to every computed total; initialise to zero.
Give a suitable test after fixing an upper boundary error. [3 marks]
Test exactly at upper boundary and one beyond, plus normal value.

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: At attempts3, >3 is false, so Open prints.

stretch.task: Fix to >=3 and add a test at attempts2.

mastery.task: Debug a login loop with a counter that sometimes resets inside the loop. Identify the fault by tracing three failures and correct it.
mastery.hint: Reset after successful login, not each failed attempt.
mastery.answer: Three wrong passwords must reach attempts3 and lock. A reset on every iteration prevents lock. Test correct login after two failures and subsequent new session.
